summary.text: The BRE flight program plans to observe burning of CH4/N2 and C2H4/N2 mixtures on porous circular burners in long-duration microgravity, under several O2/N2 atmospheres.

geometry.text: Porous circular burners of 25 and 50 mm diameter.

oxygen.text: A planned atmosphere has 21 % oxygen. Another has 26.5 % oxygen. A further atmosphere has 34 % oxygen.

pressure.text: A planned atmosphere has 14.7 psia. Another has 10.2 psia. A further atmosphere has 8.2 psia.

flow.text: Fuel flow rate is to be reduced in small increments until extinction is observed.

gravity.text: Long-duration microgravity; ignition limit tests are to be explored under normal gravity.

measurements.text: Burner surface temperature and heat flux.

claims.text: The investigation aims to observe burning behavior in long-duration microgravity for CH4/N2 and C2H4/N2 mixtures on porous circular burners of 25 and 50 mm diameter.
The investigation aims to examine an atmosphere of 14.7 psia with 21 % oxygen. Another planned atmosphere has 10.2 psia with 26.5 % oxygen. A further planned atmosphere has 8.2 psia with 34 % oxygen.
The investigation aims to consider these conditions for extinction limits.
The BRE investigation hypothesizes that there can exist a regime of quasi-steady burning in microgravity as a function of materials properties.
The source also states that steady burning may never be achieved and that only slowly changing unsteady flames may be possible.

limitations.text: Ignition limit tests are not proposed for microgravity.
The source describes its own results as preliminary; this card records no result from them.
This draft cites PSI metadata and no PDF text. The packet also includes official table passages whose findings have not been incorporated or reviewed.
